 ADVERTISEMENT   Filtered By: Weather Weather 'Danger' level heat index logged in 11 areas on Nov. 3, 2026 
 By LYJAH TIFFANY BONZO, GMA News Published November 3, 2026 6:14pm 
 Updated November 3, 2026 6:47pm + Add GMA on Google Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google. At least 11 areas across the country were monitored to be in the "danger" level heat index on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, according to state weather bureau PAGASA.
 According to PAGASA's computed heat index, the weather stations in the following places recorded heat index levels ranging from 42 to 51 degrees Celsius:
 Ilocos Region (Region 1) 
 o Dagupan City, Pangasinan — 43 degrees Celsius
o DMMMSU Bacnotan, La Union — 43 degrees Celsius

 MIMAROPA (Region 4-B) 
 San Jose, Occidental Mindoro — 42 degrees Celsius
 Cuyo, Palawan — 42 degrees Celsius
 Western Visayas (Region 6) 
 Iloilo City, Iloilo — 43 degrees Celsius
 Dumangas, Iloilo — 43 degrees Celsius
 Negros Island Region 
 La Granja, La Carlota, Negros Occidental — 43 degrees Celsius
 Siquijor, Siquijor — 42 degrees Celsius
 Eastern Visayas (Region 8) 
 Borongan, Eastern Samar — 44 degrees Celsius
 Guiuan, Eastern Samar — 42 degrees Celsius
 Caraga (Region 13) 
 Butuan City, Agusan Del Norte — 43 degrees Celsius
 Meanwhile, the following areas are forecast to experience a heat index at the danger level on Wednesday, November 4, 2026:
 43 degrees Celsius 
 Dumangas, Iloilo
 42 degrees Celsius 
 Coron, Palawan
 San Jose, Occidental Mindoro
 Cuyo, Palawan
 Borongan, Eastern Samar
 Hinatuan, Surigao del Sur
 Butuan City, Agusan del Norte
 Iloilo City, Iloilo
 La Granja, La Carlota City, Negros Occidental
 The state weather bureau warned that in areas with a heat index of 42 degrees Celsius (danger level), heat cramps, and heat exhaustion "are likely," and heat stroke "is probable with continued exposure."
 The heat index refers to the temperature felt by the human body when relative humidity is combined with actual air temperature.
 High humidity slows the evaporation of sweat, making it more difficult for the body to cool down.
 Courtesy: PAGASA 
 PAGASA advised the public to limit their time outside and use umbrellas or caps when outdoors. It also recommended drinking lots of water and avoiding the intake of tea, coffee, alcohol, and sodas.
 PAGASA typically releases heat index data during the dry season, from March until the onset of the rainy season.
 "However, the prevailing El Niño condition has urged for this off-season issuance to provide guidance for possible occurrences of associated extreme heat events," PAGASA said. — VDV/VBL, GMA News
